Our Hebrew voice model could not speak Hebrew

We ran the four ElevenLabs voice models on 12 lines we actually ship. Played back through Whisper, Multilingual v2 turned Hebrew into 53.6% character error. v4 read it at 6.4%. v3 was the best at English, and the most expensive to run.

Same voice (premade Daniel), same request body, 6 English + 6 Hebrew lines from a reel voiceover and our site's chat assistant. 54 clips, 993 credits, about $0.15.

01 / the number that matters

Character error rate after a round trip through local Whisper large-v3, lower is better. It measures whether the words survived, not whether they sound good.

Four ways to see the same result. Every number is measured; the positions of the red cells in the grid are illustrative, their count is not.

05 / how we measured without ears

An agent ran this, and an agent cannot listen. So every clip went back through speech recognition and was scored against the text it was asked to say.

06 / what this does not tell you

  • Naturalness and emotion were not measured. The players are for your ear.
  • Whisper errs on names for every model alike ("Yonyon" becomes "Yonion", RAND becomes "Rand"), and writes numbers as digits. Compare columns, not absolute values.
  • Latency is n=6 per cell, one run each, from Israel, one day after the v4 launch. One v2 call returned HTTP 429 and was retried.
  • v4's price is launch pricing, reported to end October 12 (third-party coverage, not in the official changelog when measured). Multilingual v2 billing at 0.40 credits per character, not 1.0, is unexplained.
  • The [excited] audio tag was never read aloud on v3, v4 or Turbo. On v3 the tagged Hebrew greeting lost its second half.
  • Clips on this page are re-encoded to 48 kbps mono to keep it light; the eval used 128 kbps.
